newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND CUTS THROUGH SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND CUTS THROUGH SUPPORT.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended Friday's dayside sell-off during SYCOM, cutting through a major support area of 93.360 to 93.470.
*Weakening U.S. Treasuries continue to drag local market lower, although domestic fundamentals remain superior.
The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended Friday's dayside sell-off during SYCOM, cutting through a major support area of 93.360 to 93.470.
The contract ended the Friday/Saturday after hours session at 93.290, off smartly from Friday's 93.420 pit close and was only just above a session of 93.265.

Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac Banking Corporation, expects the market will test the SYCOM low at the opening and felt that the contract was only a buy on a break back of 93.310, which could spark a 10 basis point rally.
"A more likely range is under it (93.310) and would be oversold officially at 93.200," Pontikis added.
A weakening U.S. Treasury market continues to drag local debt lower, although domestic fundamentals remain superior which should limit the market's downside.

The U.S. market sold off sharply again on Friday as concerns over economic growth increased, and faces several key economic indicators this week, including PPI and CPI. However, it could be Wednesday's retail sales data that draws the most interest in the United States as a barometer of consumer demand.

Local data is fairly thin on the ground this week, although a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in Perth on Tuesday will be keenly awaited for clues on monetary policy after the central bank's easing two weeks ago to 5.0 percent.
